ai.title: Add knowledge.md support to project context
ai.summary: System prompt now ingests `knowledge.md` files via new `knowledgeFiles` field in `ProjectFileContext`. `src/project-files.ts` filters paths ending in `knowledge.md` and loads contents, while `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` injects them into a dedicated Knowledge section. File exclusion logic in `getProjectFilePaths` now skips `.git` directories.

eli5.text: The assistant now reads a special notes file called knowledge.md that lives in your project folders and can use those notes as extra guidance when helping you. You'd notice this the next time you ask for help in a project that has a knowledge.md file: the assistant is expected to look at it, and if one is missing you may be asked (or the code nags) to add one. The change also makes the assistant stop pretending it will read a file that doesn't actually exist, so it will quit promising to show you file contents that aren't there.

ai.title: Backend prompt and frontend file handling refinements
ai.summary: System prompt clarifies file existence rules and new file creation syntax. Tools description restricts `read_files` usage to prevent redundant reads. Frontend `applyChanges` now supports creating new files with directory creation. `getFileBlocks` returns specific error markers for missing files.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to create a new file, it now automatically creates any missing folders along the way, so files can be placed in new locations without manual setup. The assistant's guidance also reminds it that files not in the project file list don't exist, and that it should only read files once unless they've changed. If a file can't be found, the error will now specifically say the file is missing instead of giving a generic message. This applies to internal tooling and is live as of the 2024-07-15 snapshot.

ai.title: Add backend knowledge.md architecture doc
ai.summary: Added backend/knowledge.md documenting Manicode backend structure. Covers TypeScript/Node stack, Express/WebSocket components, Claude integration, and file management flows. Includes development guidelines and TODOs for auth, caching, and rate limiting.

eli5.text: The team added a plain-language guide that explains how the assistant's brain works, so anyone joining the project can quickly understand how it thinks, talks, and edits files. If you peek at the project, you'd find a new 113-line guide in the backend folder that spells out each piece and leaves sticky notes (TODOs) for future improvements like login checks and speed limits.

ai.title: Refactor stop marker to constant and prevent reads of non-existent
ai.summary: The hardcoded `[END_OF_RESPONSE]` string is replaced by the `STOP_MARKER` constant exported from `common/src/prompts.ts` across backend and CLI surfaces (`backend/src/prompts.ts`, `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`, `src/index.ts`). The system prompt now explicitly instructs the agent to only read files listed in `<project_files>` and to skip `read_files` for non-existent files before editing. This mechanism change prevents tool errors from attempting to read missing files and centralizes the stop signal logic.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes writing a response, it now uses one single, shared stop signal instead of several copies of the same hardcoded text, so the system stays consistent and easier to maintain. The assistant is also being told to skip trying to open files that aren't part of the project, which prevents it from hitting errors when it looks for something that wasn't provided. For anyone watching, you won't see a dramatic change in behavior right away, but the assistant should get along a bit more smoothly without stumbling over missing files.

ai.summary: Added musings.knowledge.md containing copied Notion notes. Provides Claude additional context regarding Manicode strategy, architecture, and product ideas. Internal repo documentation only.

eli5.text: A new reference document was added internally that captures ideas about how the Manicode assistant could gather and use knowledge, written in plain language so the assistant's builders have more context when planning features. It only affects internal planning and product direction, not anything you can touch or see today. If you could open the repository, you'd see a new 151-line notes file alongside code changes that support how assistants read and act on documentation like this one.

ai.title: Fix system prompt file block template
ai.summary: Refactored hardcoded XML tags in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` to use `createFileBlock`. Replaced literal `<file>` and `</file>` strings with dynamic function calls to ensure consistent formatting. Scope limited to backend system prompt definitions. Prevents potential parsing issues by standardizing file block generation.

eli5.text: If you write instructions with file examples today, the formatting now stays uniform everywhere, removing stray text that could break how examples are parsed. This is already active for anyone reading or building those instructions, with no behavior change you would see or feel.

ai.title: Add efficient file reading instructions to system prompt
ai.summary: Appends 'Efficient File Reading and Analysis' section to `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Directs agent to check prior reads, plan file access, track gathered info, and break loops. Internal prompt tuning only.

eli5.text: The assistant behind the app got new internal notes telling it to read files carefully instead of rereading the same ones over and over. These notes only affect how the assistant works behind the scenes, so you won’t notice anything different when using the app. The guidance was added to the assistant’s instruction set on July 15, 2024, and helps prevent looping or wasted effort during complex tasks.

ai.title: musings.knowledge.md wish list
ai.summary: Added 'Wish list' section to musings.knowledge.md. Lists desired features: full terminal command access, arrow key message scrolling, and rigorous prompt testing suite. Internal documentation update only.

eli5.text: A small internal wish list was added to the team's own planning document, listing three ideas they'd like to build someday: letting the assistant run terminal commands directly, using arrow keys to scroll through past messages, and adding a thorough testing suite to check that prompts work correctly. Nothing here is live yet, so you won't notice any change in how the assistant behaves today.
